exam.title: MIT 18.06: Subspaces, Orthogonality, Eigenvalues & SVD
exam.description: College exam testing the Four Fundamental Subspaces, Gram-Schmidt QR, diagonalization, and Singular Value Decomposition.
exam.instructions: Answer all questions rigorously showing all work where applicable. Time limit: 60 minutes.

questions.text: According to the Fundamental Theorem of Linear Algebra, what is the orthogonal complement of the Row Space C(A^T) in R^n?
questions.rubric: The row space C(A^T) is orthogonal to the nullspace N(A) in R^n; every vector x in N(A) satisfies A x = 0, meaning it is perpendicular to every row of A.

questions.text: For any real symmetric matrix S (S = S^T), which statement is always TRUE?
options: All eigenvalues of S are purely imaginary.
All eigenvalues of S are real, and S can be diagonalized by an orthogonal matrix of eigenvectors (S = Q * Lambda * Q^T).
The determinant of S must be strictly positive.
The matrix S has no inverse.
questions.correct_answer: All eigenvalues of S are real, and S can be diagonalized by an orthogonal matrix of eigenvectors (S = Q * Lambda * Q^T).
questions.rubric: By the Spectral Theorem, real symmetric matrices always have real eigenvalues and an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors, yielding S = Q Lambda Q^T.

questions.text: Describe the Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) A = U * Sigma * V^T for an m x n matrix A. State what the columns of U, the diagonal of Sigma, and the columns of V represent.
questions.correct_answer: U has orthonormal eigenvectors of AA^T, V has orthonormal eigenvectors of A^TA, and Sigma has singular values sigma_i = sqrt(lambda_i).
questions.rubric: Full marks require defining U (m x m orthogonal, eigenvectors of AA^T), Sigma (m x n diagonal with singular values sigma_i >= 0), and V (n x n orthogonal, eigenvectors of A^TA).
